title: A smooth finite modification of a reduced curve
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $X$ be a reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme] separated scheme of finite type over $k$ with $\dim X\le1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Then there exist a separated scheme $X^
u$ of finite type over $k$ with $\dim X^
u\le1$ which is smooth over $k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], a finite morphism of $k$-schemes $
u:X^
u	o X$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and a dense open subscheme $X'\subseteq X$ such that $
u$ restricts to an isomorphism $
u^{-1}(X')	o X'$. (One may take for $
u$ the normalization of $X$, the disjoint union of the normalizations [def-sc-normalization] of the irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $X$ with their reduced structure.)

source.place: Varieties, Lemma 0BXR (lemma-normalization-locally-algebraic: nu finite, X^nu a disjoint union of normal irreducible schemes, nu birational for X reduced) and Lemma 0B8Y (lemma-regular-point-on-curve: normal one-dimensional over a perfect field is smooth), as used in Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 0A3Q (lemma-somewhat-easier)

proof.text:
The empty case, and the irreducible components. If $X=\emptyset$, take $X^
u=X'=\emptyset$ and $
u=\mathrm{id}$: an isomorphism is finite [lem-weil-pbc-isomorphism-finite], the empty scheme is smooth over $k$ (the conditions of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] are vacuous or trivially met on the empty scheme), separated, of finite type and of dimension $-\infty\le1$, and $\emptyset$ is dense in $\emptyset$. Assume from now on $X
eq\emptyset$. $X$ is of finite type over the field $k$, so it is covered by finitely many affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra, each Noetherian by the Hilbert basis theorem; thus $X$ is a Noetherian scheme, and by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-components] it has finitely many irreducible components $X_1,\dots,X_m$ ($m\ge1$) [def-weil-irreducible-components]. They are closed, $X=X_1\cup\cdots\cup X_m$, $X_i
ot\subseteq X_j$ for $i
eq j$, and each $X_i$ has a unique generic point $\eta_i$ (a scheme is sober); $\eta_i
otin X_j$ for $j
eq i$, since $\eta_i\in X_j$ would give $X_i=\overline{\{\eta_i\}}\subseteq X_j$. Give $X_i$ its reduced induced closed subscheme structure, with closed immersion $\iota_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$. Then $X_i$ is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme] and irreducible, hence integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]; $\iota_i$ is finite [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite], so $X_i$ (with structure morphism $X_i	o X	o\operatorname{Spec}k$) is separated and of finite type over $k$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-separated-finite-type]; and $\dim X_i\le\dim X\le1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], since a chain of irreducible closed subsets of the closed subset $X_i$ is a chain of irreducible closed subsets of $X$. As $X_i
eq\emptyset$, $\dim X_i\in\{0,1\}$.

source.place: Varieties, proof of Lemma 0BXR (lemma-normalization-locally-algebraic): $X$ locally Noetherian, finitely many irreducible components (Properties 0BA8); Morphisms, Lemma 035P (lemma-description-normalization): the normalization of a reduced $X$ is built from the irreducible components with their reduced structure

proof.text:
Components of dimension one: normalization. Let $i$ be such that $\dim X_i=1$, and let $
u_i:X_i^
u	o X_i$ be the normalization of the integral scheme $X_i$ in its function field [def-sc-normalization]. $X_i$ is an integral scheme of finite type over the field $k$, so [lem-sc-normalization-properties] applies: by (a), $
u_i$ is finite and surjective and $\dim X_i^
u=\dim X_i=1$; by (c), $X_i^
u$ is smooth over $k$, since $\dim X_i=1$ and $k$ is perfect (an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure] is perfect: in characteristic $p>0$ every $a\in k$ is a $p$-th power, being a root of $T^p-a$ has a root). By [lem-fin-dense-normal-open] the integral finite-type $k$-scheme $X_i$ has a nonempty open subscheme $U_i\subseteq X_i$ which is normal, and by (b) of [lem-sc-normalization-properties] the induced morphism $
u_i^{-1}(U_i)=X_i^
u	imes_{X_i}U_i	o U_i$ is an isomorphism. $X_i^
u$ is a $k$-scheme through $X_i^
u	o X_i	o\operatorname{Spec}k$, so $
u_i$ is a $k$-morphism.

source.place: Varieties, Lemma 0BXR (1), (3) (finite, birational) and Lemma 0B8Y (normal points of a curve over a perfect field are smooth points), as used in Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 0A3Q

proof.text:
Components of dimension zero. Let $i$ be such that $\dim X_i=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-zero-dim-integral-point] the structure morphism $X_i	o\operatorname{Spec}k$ is an isomorphism. Put $X_i^
u:=X_i$, $
u_i:=\mathrm{id}_{X_i}$, which is finite [lem-weil-pbc-isomorphism-finite], and $U_i:=X_i$, over which $
u_i$ is trivially an isomorphism. $X_i^
u	o\operatorname{Spec}k$ is an isomorphism, hence smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]: it is of finite presentation ($k	o k$ is), and formally smooth, since for a first-order thickening $T\subset T'$ over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $a:T	o X_i$ over $k$, the morphism $T'	o\operatorname{Spec}k\cong X_i$ restricts to $a$ on $T$ (both are the structure morphism of $T$ followed by the inverse isomorphism). $\dim X_i^
u=0$. (This agrees with the normalization of $X_i\cong\operatorname{Spec}k$, which is normal, by (b) of [lem-sc-normalization-properties]; the identity is used to avoid the dimension-one hypothesis of its part (c).)

source.place: Varieties, Lemma 0BXR (1) ($\nu$ finite, $X^\nu$ a disjoint union of normal irreducible schemes); Morphisms, Lemmas 01WK (composition of finite morphisms) and 0CYI (finite disjoint union of finite morphisms)

proof.text: The dense open $X'$ (topology). For each $i$ let $W_i:=X\setminus\bigcup_{j\neq i}X_j$, open in $X$ (finite union of closed sets), contained in $X_i$ (as $X=\bigcup_jX_j$), and containing $\eta_i$ (step 1). Let $V_i:=U_i\cap W_i$ with $U_i\subseteq X_i$ the open of steps 2, 3. $V_i$ is open in $X$: $U_i$ is open in $X_i$, so $U_i\cap W_i$ is open in the subspace $W_i$ of $X_i$, and $W_i$ is open in $X$. $V_i$ is nonempty: $U_i$ and $W_i=W_i\cap X_i$ are nonempty open subsets of the irreducible space $X_i$, so they meet; consequently $\eta_i\in V_i$ (a nonempty open subset of $X_i$ contains its generic point). For $i\neq j$, $V_i\cap V_j=\emptyset$, since $V_i\subseteq W_i$ is disjoint from $X_j\supseteq V_j$. Put $X':=V_1\cup\cdots\cup V_m=V_1\amalg\cdots\amalg V_m$, an open subset of $X$, with the open subscheme structure. $X'$ is dense in $X$: its closure contains every $\eta_i$, hence every $X_i=\overline{\{\eta_i\}}$, hence $X$.

split_report.summary: Split in six steps following Stacks 0BXR/0B8Y/035P/0BAJ as used in 0A3Q: empty case and irreducible components with reduced structure (integral, separated finite type, dim <= 1); dimension-one components normalized via lem-sc-normalization-properties (a) finite, dim preserved, (c) smooth (k perfect), (b) iso over a nonempty normal open from lem-fin-dense-normal-open; dimension-zero components are Spec k (new unsplit lem-weil-pbc-zero-dim-integral-point) and are kept with the identity; assembly of X^nu = disjoint union with nu finite (new Mathlib leaves lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition, lem-weil-pbc-finite-coproduct), separated finite type (new leaf lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-separated-finite-type), smooth (new leaf lem-weil-pbc-smooth-coproduct), dim <= 1; the dense open X' = disjoint union of U_i minus the other components, and nu an isomorphism over it (elementary, written out). Added def-pc-reduced-scheme and def-weil-irreducible-components to stmt_deps. Off-route statements used as tools: lem-fin-dense-normal-open (unit sk-prop-a1-kummer) and lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-components (unit sk-prop-sf-cbc).
